A first-in-human T-cell engager (TCE) study starts orders of magnitude
below the biologically active dose and climbs toward it one cohort at a
time. This project collects the ways of climbing faster, and works each
one out far enough to say where it applies and what it saves.

## Approaches

| Approach | What it changes | Where it applies | Status here |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 1. Intrapatient dose escalation, with single-patient cohorts | Climbs the ladder within one patient rather than one cohort per rung | Any indication; the value rises with uncertainty about the active dose | Specified as a simulation, not built |
| 2. Healthy volunteer escalation | Finds the active dose in volunteers before the first patient is enrolled | Autoimmune indications with a B-cell or plasma-cell target; closed in oncology | Registry search done, three studies found, none reported |
| 3. MABEL starting dose | Starts higher, on a better prediction of the active dose | Any indication | Out of scope, since it is widely practised; entry 2 of the references is the pointer |

: The three approaches, and how far each has been taken here {tbl-colwidths="[26,28,28,18]"}

The three are not exclusive. A better starting dose shrinks the gap the
other two cross, and a volunteer study, where it is open, is a
starting-dose method with human data behind it.

## Documents

- [Working specification](specification.qmd). Approach 1. The design,
  the PK and pharmacodynamic models, the endpoints, and the
  implementation sequence for the intrapatient escalation simulation.
  Its **In brief** section is one screen and says what the rest argues;
  its Section 1 carries the fork between approaches 1 and 2.
- [T-cell engagers in healthy volunteers](tce-hv.qmd). Approach 2. The
  three registered volunteer studies, all autoimmune and all since
  December 2025, what a volunteer study can measure, the translation to
  patients, and a speed estimate under stated assumptions.
- [References](references.qmd). What to read and in what order, for
  approaches 1 and 2, and a marker on every source recording whether its
  use here has been checked. Approach 3's pointer is entry 2.
- [MCLA-117 notes](mcla117-notes.qmd). The published Cycle 1 escalation
  scheme the specification cites as precedent, its dose tables, and the
  four features of it that bear on the design.
- [Simon 1997 reading notes](simon97-notes.qmd). What the accelerated
  titration designs paper reports when intrapatient escalation is switched on
  and off, with every number sourced to a page.

## Code

- `make_escalation_figure.py` draws `mcla117-escalation.svg`, the Cycle 1
  escalation figure in Section 6 of the specification. Plain Python with no
  plotting library, so the site build never runs it. Run it after changing the
  dose table it carries.
